transcription.text: Converting public records into digital files can make information easier to locate, but accessibility is not achieved simply by scanning documents. Search systems depend on accurate descriptions, readable text, and consistent information about when and how each record was created. A badly indexed collection can remain effectively invisible, even when every page is online. Long-term preservation presents another challenge, because software formats and storage systems eventually become obsolete. Institutions need procedures for checking files, migrating them to suitable formats, and documenting any changes made during that process. They must also consider which personal details should be restricted and which records serve a legitimate public interest. The objective is durable and intelligible access, supported by clear responsibilities, rather than the rapid accumulation of files that nobody can reliably interpret.
